title: Cut the stamp duty surcharge on additional homes back to 3%
description: Autumn Budget 2024 raised the stamp duty surcharge on second homes and buy-to-let purchases from 3 to 5 percentage points. Switch this on to return it to 3 points from April 2027, giving up the Treasury's costing (£0.3bn in 2029-30).

baselinePolicy.text: Higher rates for additional dwellings 5 percentage points above the standard rates since 31 October 2024 (Autumn Budget 2024, Table 5.1 line 25).

lines.title: Stamp Duty Land Tax (SDLT): Increase the Higher Rate of Additional Dwelling (HRAD) of SDLT by 2ppts from 3% to 5% from 31 October 2024

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury's costing with its sign reversed for 2027-28 to 2029-30; 2030-31 carries the 2029-30 figure forward with the OBR's capital taxes receipts path.

uprating.head: capitalTaxes
uprating.note: Applied in the years the scorecard covers and extended to 2030-31 with the OBR's capital taxes receipts (ADR-0004).

caveats: The Treasury's costing is on the OBR's October 2024 forecast and reflects the property market then expected; the level is not rebased.

considerations.text: The Treasury's scorecard figure is the certified costing of the surcharge rise, including the transactions response the Treasury and OBR agreed.

interactions.text: Both change stamp duty on residential purchases; HMRC's band figures are for main homes and the surcharge applies on top.
